Briefly stated that the case of the prosecution against the accused persons is that accused Sumit (since expired) and accused Krishna on 03.11.2008, at H.No. A 1/29 Shiv Vihar Delhi dishonestly induced complainant Shakil Beg to purchase the aforesaid property by representing themselves as the owner of the same and obtained Rs. 4 lacs as consideration and again in the same manner by representing themselves as owner of abovesaid property on 25.12.2008, they obtained Rs. 1 lakhs as earnest money from Ram Vilas Mehto qua abovesaid property.
Further, all accused persons on 24.12.2008, committed house trespass at H. No. A-1/29, Shiv Vihar, Karala with intention to commit cheating.
On this basis, the present FIR was registered against the accused persons.

sentences.text: 2.The Ld. Predecessor of this court took cognizance of the offence and issued process against the accused persons.
Pursuant to the appearance of the accused persons, they were supplied with the copy of the chargesheet in compliance with Section 207 CrPC.
3.Thereafter, charge under section 420/451/34 IPC was framed against the accused persons.

The accused persons pleaded not guilty and the matter was listed for Prosecution Evidence ('PE').
4.Accused Sumit Kumar expired during trial and proceedings against him stood abated.
5.In order to establish its case against the accused, prosecution has examined the following witnesses:-
6.PW1 Smt. Nirmala deposed that 2-3 years before, she had given Rs. 75000/- to accused Sumit (since expired) who was residing in his neighbourhood.
She further deposed when she cross examined by ld. APP for the State that she know accused persons before the court being her neighbour.

She further admitted that accused Sumit Kumar resided at H. No. E-50, Shiv Vihar,
Karala, Delhi.
The witness was cross examined by Ld APP for the State wherein she denied her statement Mark A in totality and did not support the case of the prosecution.
The witness was not cross examined by Ld. counsel for the accused persons despite the opportunity given.
7.PW2 Sh. Shakil Baig deposed that at the time of incident in 2008, he was residing at 1/29, Shiv Vihar Karala and on 02.11.2008, he went to the office of property dealer Bharat Kumar at Karla.

PW2 further deposed the real brother of Bharat Kumar namely Yashpal Gilani works with PW2 as driver and when he visited the property shop, he met with accused Krishna along with her husband/co-accused Sumit (Since expired) as both accused persons were present in connection with the sale of their house bearing no. A-1/29, Khasra No.88/16/2 at Shiv Vihar and PW2 showed interest in the said property and also visited the said house and finalized the deal with both accused persons.

PW2 further deposed that on 03.11.2008, he gave a cheque of Rs. 4 lakhs to accused Sumit Kumar and the same was encashed by accused Sumit Kumar and thereafter, accused Sumit Kumar executed GPA, Will and receipts, documents in the favour of PW2.
PW2 further deposed that the accused also handed over the original documents as well as previous chain of ownership of said house to him and also handed over the possession of said house itself.
PW2 further deposed that accused persons vacated the said house and started residing at E Block Shiv Vihar on rent and PW2 started living in their house.

PW2 further deposed that on 23.12.2008, he went to his native village at Badaun, U.P. and his driver Yashpal was aware about this fact and from him, property dealer Bharat Kumar, accused Sumit Kumar and accused Krishna were also aware that PW2 has gone out of station.

PW2 further deposed that on 29.12.2008, he received a call from property dealer Bharat that accused Sumit had got prepared duplicate keys of his house in collusion with accused Krishna and brother in law Rajesh and some of neighbours also informed PW2 that accused persons have stated to them that they have again purchased the said property and looking for a prospective buyer.

PW2 further deposed that he was also informed that all accused persons had obtained bayana State vs Krishana on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159767547/
2 amount from one Ram Vilas Metho and they all left the area.

PW2 deposed that he immediately on 30.12.2008, reached at his house and called the police however, before the arrival of police, one Mahender Singh alongwith his son Parvesh Kumar arrived at the said house and claimed to be the actual owner of the house of PW2 and that they had purchased the same from accused Krishna.
PW2 further deposed that he disclosed to Mahender Singh that he had purchased the property from accused Krishna @ Guddi @ Premlat on 12.12.2007 after completion of all documentation.
PW2 further deposed that Mahender forcefully put his lock on the property in question and they both produce the complete chain of documents in the police station.

PW2 further deposed that on verification of property documents, it was found that the documents given to PW2 by accused persons are forged and fabricated and the documents of Mahender were correct one.

PW2 further deposed that accused persons Krishna and Sumit cheated him on the basis of false and fabricated documents of property and did not hand over original and true chain of the property in question in order to cheat him.
PW2 further deposed that on 30.12.2008, he made a call to police and vigilance inquiry was conducted by IO Parveen Kumar.

PW2 further deposed that he made a complaint EX.
PW2/A, entire chain of property in question, his written complaint made to police commissioner Ex.
PW2/B to the police.
Further, he correctly identified accused Krishna and Rajesh in the court.
The witness was duly cross examined by Ld. counsel for the accused persons.
8.PW3 Mahender deposed that he had purchased a plot of 60 Sq.Yards bearing no. A-1/29, Khasra No.88/16/2 at Shiv Vihar colony from accused Krishna on 12.12.2007 for a sum of Rs. 60,000/-.

PW3 further deposed that accused Krishna purchased the same from one Ram Akshay and presently he is having the possession of said property and he had put his locks on the same and police recorded his statement and during investigation, he showed the property document and handed over the photocopy of the same to police.
Further, he correctly identified the accused Krishna in the court.

He was cross examined by Ld. APP for the State wherein, he admitted his statement Ex.
PW3/A was recorded by police officials, that accused Krishna and her husband Sumit (since expired) started residing at property in question on rent.
He further admitted that accused Krishna alongwith her husband sold the property in question to one Shakeel on the basis of false and fabricated documents.
The witness was cross examined by Ld. counsel for the accused persons.

9.PW4 Sh. Bharat Kumar deposed that on 02.11.2008, he used to work in the factory of Sumit and he showed his intention to sell his plot and accordingly, PW4 introduced him to Sh. Shakil who was a friend of his brother and the deal was confirmed for Rs. 4 lakh as total consideration.
PW4 further deposed that relevant papers were prepared and signed by both the parties after receiving the cheque and physical possession was also handed over to Mr. Shakil by Sumit.

PW4 further deposed that on 24.12.2008, he came to know that brother in law of Sumit has taken the possession of premises in question and on 29.12.2008, Shakil came at the spot and lodged the report and later he also came to know Sumit got prepared the keys of the house from someone.
The witness was duly cross examined by Ld. counsel for the accused persons.

10.PW5 Sh. Sanjeev Jain proved notary record dt. 03.11.2008 whereby he notarized the documents i.e., GPA, Will and receipt, possession letter, agreement to sell and made entry in this regard in the register at serial no. 4006 & 4007 Ex. PW5/A.
The witness was not cross examined by Ld. counsel for the accused persons despite the opportunity given.

PW6 further deposed that he searched the accused persons, recorded the statement of witnesses, arrested the accused Sumit (Since expired) on 31.01.2010 from Chundi Naka, Nosara,

He further deposed that on 23.02.2010, he arrested that accused Rajesh in the PS vide memo Ex. PW6/B and on 20.03.2010, he arrested the accused Krishna from H.No. 354, Village Majid Mot, Delhi vide arrest memo Ex.PW6/C and personally searched accused Sumit and Rajesh Ex. PW6/D and PW6/E.
PW6 further deposed that he also moved application for getting journey warrant of accused Sumit before Gonda, U.P. Ex. PW6/F.

PW2 further deposed that photocopies of GPA, agreement to sale, affidavit and receipt executed by Ramesh Kumar and Ram Asre Das are Mark 6A (Colly) and documents executed by Sumit Kumar are Mark 6B (Colly).
He further mentioned that he recorded the disclosure statement of accused Sumit Ex. PW6/F.
Further witness correctly identified the accused Krishna and Rajesh in the court.
The witness was cross examined by Ld. counsel for the accused persons.

12. PW7 Inspector Parveen Kumar that one complaint of complainant Sh. PW7 further proved his report Ex.

The witness was not cross examined by the Ld. counsel for the accused persons despite opportunity given.

13. PW8 Ram Vilas Mehto deposed that on 24.12.2008, his sister in law Nirmala told him that accused Sumit is selling its property bearing no. A-1/29, Khasra No.88/16/2 at Shiv Vihar colony and thereafter, they both went to meet Sumit Kumar and his wife and they showed interest in PIQ and deal was finalized for Rs. 8 lakh.
PW8 further deposed that on 25.12.2008, he gave Rs. 1 lakh as token money and received receipt Ex.
PW8 / A.
PW8 further deposed that the accused taken Rs. 1 lakhs in January 2009 and remaining amount of Rs.6 lakhs was to be paid up to 10.06.2009.
PW8 further deposed that accused persons Sumit and Krishna had taken his money and thereafter, they were not found anywhere.
Further witness correctly identified the accused Krishna in the court.
The witness was cross examined by Ld. counsel for accused persons.
14.Thereafter, vide order dated 25.04.2025, PE was closed.
15.In the statement recorded u/s. 313 CrPC, accused persons denied the case of the prosecution and pleaded innocence.
They stated that they have been falsely implicated in the present case.
Accused Rajesh did not opt to lead defence evidence.
However, accused Krishna opted to lead defence evidence.
16. Accused Krishna stepped into the witness box and examined herself as DW1 and deposed that her husband expired two days before Diwali in the year 2017.
She also produced one loan agreement between Sumit Kumar and complainant Shakeel Baig executed on 03.11.2008 Ex. DW1/A (OSR).
She was cross examined by Ld. APP for the State.

sentences.text: 17.Ld. APP for the state has submitted that the prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubt as the witnesses have identified the accused persons and have corroborated each other in material particulars.

18.Per contra, Ld. Counsel for the accused persons has submitted that the accused persons are innocent and deserve the benefit of the doubt for the following reasons:-
18.1. Accused persons belong to a very poor strata of the society whereas the complainants are property dealers/money lenders who have trapped the accused persons.
18.2. The accused persons had taken a loan from complainant Shakeel Beg and in lieu of that they were forced to execute various documents.
Being uneducated and in dire need of money they executed those documents without being aware of the contents.
The complainant is claiming ownership over the property on the basis of those documents.
The complainant categorically declined during his cross-examination that he never gave any loan to the accused persons.
However, he has failed to explain the contemporaneous execution of a loan document of the same amount.
18.3. The accused persons have produced the loan agreement as Ex DW1/1 bearing the signatures of the complainant Shakeel Beg.
18.4. As far as the case of Ram Vilas Mehto is concerned, it has been totally thrashed by his sister in law Nirmala, who declined the entire transaction.
Even if there were some transactions between Sumit and Ram Vilas Mehto, his wife Krishna cannot be held liable for the same.
19.Before discussing the testimonies of PWs, it would be prudent to discuss the legal position involved in the present case.

Legal Framework 20.Section 420 IPC provides :-
"Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything which is signed or sealed, and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine."
State vs Krishana on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159767547/
5 Section 451 IPC provides :-
"Whoever commits house-trespass in order to the committing of any offence punishable with imprisonment, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, and shall also be liable to fine;
And if the offence intended to be committed is theft, the term of the imprisonment may be extended to seven years."
21.Now, coming to the facts of the present case.
Whether the prosecution has proved beyond reasonable doubt that the accused persons cheated complainant Shakeel Beg.
22.As far as the offence of cheating is concerned, PW Shakeel Beg supported the case of the prosecution against accused Sumit (since expired) and accused Krishna.
No allegation qua cheating or inducement was made against accused Rajesh.

However, accused Krishna has taken the defence that they had only taken a loan of Rs 4 lakhs from the complainant Shakeel Beg and were made to execute certain documents without understanding their contents.
The prosecution failed to produce the original documents executed by accused Sumit in favour of complainant Shakeel Beg.
Only the photocopy of such documents was produced by PW6 as Mark 6B.
No reason for failure to produce the original documents has been explained by the prosecution.

Even if the said defect is ignored, the said document Mark 6B is between accused Sumit (since expired) and complainant Shakil Beg and does not bear the signatures/thumb impressions of accused Krishna.
There is no specific averment against accused Krishna apart from the fact that she had accompanied accused Sumit being his wife.
23.Further
, the prosecution has utterly failed to explain the existence of Ex DW1/A i.e. a loan agreement between Shakil Beg and Sumit for a sum of Rs 4 lakhs.
The loan agreement Ex DW1/A and Mark 6B both are dated 03.11.2008.
Upon a prima facie comparison, the signatures of Shakil Beg on the two documents also appear to be similar.
PW Shakil Beg has categorically denied giving any loan to Krishna or Sumit.

This denial when juxtaposed with Ex DW1/A raises a significant doubt regarding the credibility of PW Shakil Beg.
24.I
have also carefully considered the testimony of PW4 Bharat Kumar.
PW4 Bharat Kumar has supported PW Shakil Beg.
However, it is quite interesting to note that PW4 Bharat Kumar has admitted during his cross-examination that he had given few cheques of Rs 1 lakh to Shakil Beg which had been dishonoured.
He also admitted to knowing Shakeel Beg for more than 20 years.
Moreover, Shakeel Beg has also identified Bharat Kumar as a property dealer and the brother of his driver in his examination-in-chief.
Therefore, the possibility of Bharat Kumar being an interested witness cannot be negated.

25.All these circumstances when considered together in the context provided by the accused that they have been framed by a nexus of money lenders and property dealers, do give rise to a substantial doubt in favour of the accused persons.

sentences.text: Therefore, this court is of the considered view that the prosecution has failed to establish beyond reasonable doubt that the accused Krishna and Rajesh had cheated complainant Shakil Beg.
Whether the prosecution has proved beyond reasonable doubt that the accused persons cheated Ram Vilas Mehto.
26.PW8 Ram Vilas Mehto has supported the case of the prosecution.
He produced a bayana receipt Ex PW8/A to show that he had paid Rs 1 lakh to accused Sumit (since expired).
Admittedly there is no signature of accused Krishna on this document.
Moreover, the PW1 Nirmala has completely denied the case of the prosecution.
She has specifically denied her thumb impressions on Ex PW8/A (Mark B).
Although she stated that she had given Rs 75,000/- to accused Sumit but categorically denied that PW8 Ram Vilas Mehto had paid Rs 1 lakh to accused Sumit or executed any bayana agreement.

27.Even if the version of PW 8 Ram Vilas Mehto is presumed to be true, the prosecution has utterly failed to prove the existence of dishonest intention on the part of accused Sumit (since expired) or accused Sumit and his wife accused Krishna.
It is pertinent to observe that the prosecution has failed to prove that accused Sumit and Krishna had already sold the property to either Mahender Kumar or Shakeel Beg.
PW Mahender Kumar failed to show any original document through which he had obtained the possession of the property.
He also failed to bring any documentary evidence that he had inducted accused Sumit and Krishna on rent in the said property.
In fact, during his cross-examination, he admitted that he had never provided any documents to the police related to the property in question.
The sale made to Shakeel Beg has already been held to be dubious by me in the preceding paras.
Once prior sale remains unproved, the dispute between Ram Vilas Mehto and Sumit appears to be merely one of breach of agreement having civil consequences.
28.The
distinction between breach of contract and an offence of cheating is very fine.
It depends upon the intention of the accused at the time of inducement which can be judged by a subsequent conduct but, the subsequent conduct itself cannot be the sole test.
It is trite law, that for attracting the offence of cheating, there shall be a dishonest or fraudulent intention at the time of making the representation.
If a person fails subsequently to keep up his promise, it would not mean that he had culpable intention not to fulfil his part of the contract or to keep his promise subsequently.

It was held in S.V.L. Murthy etc. v State (2009) 6 SCC 77, by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India that for the purpose of constituting an offence of cheating, the complainant is required to show that the accused had fraudulent or dishonest intention at the time of making promise or representation.

entities.text: S.V.L. Murthy etc. v State (2009) 6 SCC 77
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even in a case where allegations are made in regard to failure on the part of the accused to keep his promise, in the absence of a culpable intention at the time of making the initial promise being absent, no offence under Section 420 of the Penal Code can be said to have been made out.
29.Looking at the facts of the present case, there is not even an iota of indication let alone evidence that there was a fraudulent or dishonest intention at the time of making the promise.
Therefore, this court comes to the irresistible conclusion that the prosecution has failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that the accused persons had cheated Ram Vilas Mehto.

sentences.text: Whether the prosecution has proved that the accused persons had criminally trespassed in the property in question on 24.12.2008 30.
As already discussed, the prosecution has failed to prove that the accused persons had sold the property to Shakeel Beg or Mahender Kumar.
Neither has the prosecution sufficiently proved that the property was in possession of Shakeel Beg on 24.12.2008.
Therefore, the question of criminal trespass does not arise.
Even otherwise, the entire evidence on this point is merely hearsay as none of the witnesses have seen the accused persons entering the property.
As per PW Shakeel Beg he was informed by PW Bharat Kumar that the accused persons have got prepared duplicate keys of the property.
Whereas, as per PW Bharat Kumar, he was also informed by some neighbours that the accused persons have got prepared the duplicate keys.
Further, he stated during his cross-examination, that he never inquired from whom the accused persons had got prepared the duplicate keys neither any investigation has been done on this point.
Accordingly, the case of the prosecution has failed on this point as well.
31.Thus

, in view of the foregoing analysis, this court is of the considered opinion that there are sufficient grounds to raise a doubt on the veracity of the entire prosecution case against the accused persons and extend the benefit of doubt to them.

Therefore, the accused Krishna, W/o Late Sh.
Sumit Kumar and Rajesh, S/o Sh. Jag Prasad are held not guilty and stand acquitted of the offence punishable under section 420/451/34 IPC.
